task: Crash-proof / pausable / resumable 24/7 develop-loop training infrastructure (owner's HARD prerequisite for the foundational-curriculum training).

owner_bar.2_cannot_be_accidentally_killed: survives terminal-close / parent-exit; auto-restart on crash
owner_bar.3_pausable_on_demand: owner wants to game -> free the GPU gracefully -> resume later
owner_bar.4_crash_resumable_bounded_loss: atomic + frequent checkpoints; resume-from-latest; NO corruption on hard kill; NO start-from-scratch

verdict: GO — training is crash-proof / pausable / resumable to the owner's bar. The existing per-day persist/resume was already atomic+correct; the hardening adds fsync-durability, a PAUSE sentinel, a heartbeat, and a detached auto-restart watchdog. All four requirements validated on CPU (numpy), NO sim/ edit, NO GPU contention. Residual (honest): intra-DAY checkpointing is not byte-level (a hard kill loses the in-flight day's partial work, not completed days) — bounded to MINUTES via --max-windows-per-day; full intra-day stream-cortex cp_connections persistence is a documented GPU follow-on.

already_robust: BridgeLineage.save() is ATOMIC: writes current.simstate.h5.new then os.replace() (Windows-safe atomic rename) -> a reader never sees a torn checkpoint (sim/lineage.py:216-225). metadata.json likewise (.new + os.replace, sim/lineage.py:177-186).
_save_state persists the FULL DevelopState every day (day, facts, vocab, current_tier, metrics, turns) as JSON via the lineage save_fn (_longitudinal_develop_loop.py:427-451).

develop_gpu(resume=True) correctly reloads DevelopState, re-instates facts (re-teach), re-hears cumulative vocab to re-acquire learned codes, and continues from state.day (_longitudinal_develop_loop_gpu.py:312-339). CLAUDE.md 'lived 5 more days on a resume' reproduced.
Verified: save->reload->resume continues from the correct day with facts/vocab preserved (no corruption).
gaps_found_and_closed: (a) NO fsync before the atomic rename: os.replace guarantees no torn read but NOT that the renamed file's bytes are on physical media before a power loss. CLOSED: supervisor _fsync_lineage() fsyncs current.simstate.h5 + metadata.json + the dir entry after each day's save (develop_loop_supervisor.py:_fsync_lineage).
(b) NO pause mechanism. CLOSED: PAUSE sentinel polled at each day boundary -> clean exit 42.

(c) NO watchdog that restarts the TRAINING (repo's autonomous_watchdog.ps1 restarts the Claude CLI, not the run). CLOSED: scripts/develop_train_watchdog.ps1 owns the training process, auto-restarts on crash, respects PAUSE.
(d) NO run-detached launcher (survives terminal close). CLOSED: scripts/start_develop_training.ps1 launches the watchdog detached.

(e) BUG found during testing: routing PAUSE through develop_gpu's per_day_save_hook did NOT stop the loop — the loop deliberately SWALLOWS hook exceptions ('a save must never kill the develop loop'), so a raised pause was caught and the loop ran away (observed: ran to day 10 with PAUSE set). FIXED: added an additive should_continue() predicate to develop_gpu, polled at the TOP of each day (the correct deterministic pause seam); default None = byte-identical.

files.research/runners/develop_loop_supervisor: NEW. The crash-proof/pausable/resumable supervisor around develop_gpu (PUBLIC seams only). run_resumable(): runs unbounded days into one persistent lineage, fsyncs every checkpoint (_fsync_lineage), writes a heartbeat.json, polls the PAUSE sentinel + an optional runtime cap via should_continue() at each day boundary, re-hears cumulative vocab on resume. PAUSE_EXIT_CODE=42.
files.research/runners/_longitudinal_develop_l: EDIT (+17/-1, runner not sim/): additive should_continue=None param on develop_gpu, polled BEFORE each day -> clean stop without starting the next day. Default None = byte-identical (verified: the runner's own smoke is GO unchanged; all other callers pass None implicitly).
files.scripts/develop_train_watchdog.ps1: NEW. The training watchdog: while PAUSE set -> hold (GPU free); else run the supervisor foreground; on exit 42 (pause/runtime-cap) -> do NOT restart; on any other exit (crash/kill) -> restart from the last checkpoint after a backoff. MaxRestarts=0 = unlimited (24/7).
files.scripts/start_develop_training.ps1: NEW. Launches the watchdog DETACHED (Start-Process -WindowStyle Hidden -PassThru) so it survives the terminal closing; writes bridges/developed/.train_watchdog.pid.
files.research/runners/_curriculum_kill_safety: NEW. The decisive kill-safety gate (hard-kill mid-run + integrity + resume).
NEW. The PAUSE-sentinel test (mid-run pause + clean exit 42 + resume).

hardening.checkpoint_cadence: per-DAY, atomic (.new + os.replace) + fsync'd (durable to physical disk). --max-windows-per-day bounds a day's wall-clock -> bounds worst-case crash loss to that day's minutes. The supervisor also exposes --max-runtime-s for optional lossless process recycling.
hardening.pause_mechanism: a PAUSE sentinel file (default bridges/PAUSE), polled by should_continue() at each day boundary. On presence: the current day finishes + is durably persisted, then the loop stops cleanly with exit 42; the watchdog sees 42 and does NOT restart (returns to pause-wait, GPU free).
hardening.watchdog: scripts/develop_train_watchdog.ps1 (+ scripts/start_develop_training.ps1 for detached launch). Distinct from the repo's autonomous_watchdog.ps1 (which restarts Claude). Reuses the project's watchdog PATTERN (a long-lived supervisor loop + a sentinel/lock).

kill_safety.method: establish 2 days -> relaunch unbounded -> taskkill /F /T mid-run (a day in flight) -> check integrity -> relaunch -> assert resume + continue.
kill_safety.worst_case_loss: <= the single in-flight (unfinished) day; 0 completed days re-done

watchdog_pause_respect.observed: while PAUSE set, watchdog logs 'PAUSE sentinel present -> training held (gaming)' every poll and NEVER launches the supervisor (GPU stays free).

honest_residual: Intra-DAY checkpoint granularity: a hard kill loses the IN-FLIGHT day's partial stream-learning (completed days are never lost; resume re-does only the unfinished day). Mitigated to MINUTES via --max-windows-per-day. Byte-level intra-day persistence would require persisting the stream-cortex cp_connections mid-day — a documented GPU follow-on (the loop currently re-hears the cumulative vocab on resume to re-instate codes).
The directory-entry fsync is best-effort (not supported on all Windows configs); the atomic rename (os.replace) stands regardless, so a torn read is impossible even without the dir fsync.
All robustness tests run on CPU (numpy) to avoid GPU contention; the persistence/pause/watchdog logic is backend-independent (it operates on the lineage JSON/.h5 + process lifecycle, not the GPU).
